author: श्रीराघवेन्द्रस्वामी
commentary: अस्त्वेवमात्मनो नित्यत्वं, अथाऽपि देहयोगवियोगरूपजनिमृती स्त एव । युद्धे च मृतिर्नियता। अतस्तन्निमित्तं च दुःखं मदीयानां भविष्यतीति मे शोक इत्यत आह ॥ अथ चेति ॥ नित्यशब्दोऽत्रावधारणे । एनं जीवं नित्यजातं देहयोगरूपजनिमन्तमेव, नित्यं मृतं देहवियोगरूपमृतिमन्तमेव त्वं मन्यसे चेत्तथाऽपि हे महाबहो एनं जीवं शोचितुं नार्हसीत्यर्थः ॥ २.२६॥
translation:
Or if thou thinkest of him as ever born or as ever dead, even then, O mighty armed, it is not fit that thou grievest. (26) 
V. Ever (Nitya) here adds emphasis. The first clause means ‘If thou shouldst think of him as having birth alone’. The second means ‘Or if thou shouldst think of him as having death alone, i.e., if once dead he is dead for ever). In either case no reason for grief is seen, for each is inevitable according to his own hypothesis. (26.) 
A. In the preceding verse the first half states the doubt of Arjuna, and the second half his grief is groundless. But how groundless, it has not been stated. The next verse gives the reason with the conclusion that birth and death inevitably succeed each other till Moksha is obtained.
